faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: GeoATM is an intelligent cash-access platform. It combines a directory of more than {atms} ATM locations with live availability reported by participating institutions, so you can find the best place to withdraw cash — not just the nearest pin.
faq.q2: How does GeoATM know if cash is available?
faq.a2: Participating institutions publish live status for their machines directly to GeoATM, and GeoATM shows it as operator reported. Where a machine isn't yet part of a live feed, it's shown from public map data and clearly marked as estimated — GeoATM never claims a live cash status it can't confirm.
faq.a3: Yes. Finding ATMs and checking availability in the consumer app is free, everywhere GeoATM operates.
faq.a4: Banks, ATM operators, processors and central banks can join the GeoATM network to publish live availability and gain visibility. Register your institution online: we verify your organisation, then your 30-day free trial of Monitor starts. Central banks and associations can write to us.
faq.a5: GeoATM's directory maps more than {atms} ATM locations in {countries} countries and territories. Operator-reported live availability expands as more institutions join the network.

operators.monitorTitle: Monitor: your network, day to day

availability.title: Availability
availability.body: Uptime and history for every ATM, from the daily status report you already produce. On every plan, Free included.

exceptions.title: Exceptions
exceptions.body: Machines offline in several reports running, statuses that keep flipping, machines missing from your latest report, and reports that have stopped.

competitors.title: Competitor locations
competitors.body: Other institutions' ATMs within 500 m and 1 km of yours, your most contested sites, and two networks compared side by side. Locations only: never another bank's status or data.

customers.title: Customer issues
customers.body: When customers say an ATM had no cash or was out of service, you see it against the status you reported. This grows as more people use GeoATM.

listings.title: Your listings against the public record
listings.body: ATMs missing from the public map, placed in the wrong spot or listed twice, listings under your name that aren't in your inventory, and hours that differ. Your administrators hear of new findings by email, at most once a day.

osm.title: Fix the public map, not just your records
osm.body: Send a finding about your own ATM to OpenStreetMap as a note for local mappers to check, after seeing exactly what it will say.

operators.intelligenceTitle: Intelligence: planning where to go next

coverage.title: Coverage analysis
coverage.body: Areas where people searched and found no ATM within the distance you choose (5, 10, 15, 20 km or your own), against the ATMs mapped today, with the gaps near your network on your own map.

expansion.title: Expansion comparisons
expansion.body: Up to five candidate sites in one country, side by side: the searches around each, your nearest ATM and the institutions already there.

network.title: Network comparisons
network.body: Up to five institutions in any country: footprint, overlap and the areas where rivals are and you aren't.

demand.title: Demand indicators
demand.body: Searches counted by area of about 2 km, month by month. Areas with fewer than three searches in a month are never shown.

excel.title: Excel downloads
excel.body: Every comparison (networks, sites and, on Enterprise, the regional benchmark) and the demand figures, downloadable to Excel for your board and planning teams.

operators.intelligenceNote: Search counts come from people using GeoATM and grow with use; we hold no footfall or transaction data. Paid from activation, and we're happy to give you a demonstration first: {email}
operators.sharingTitle: Share with associations and regulators, on your terms
operators.sharingLead: Powered by <gt></gt>, GeoATM enables secure, consent-based data sharing with banking associations, regulators and other authorised organisations. You control what information is shared, with whom, for what purpose and for how long. Permissions can be revoked, and every sharing action is recorded.
operators.sharingAlt: Two phones showing the GeoATM operator portal: a bank granting a payments forum consent to see its status and history, and a banking association's Shared with me screen with the bank's consent and what it passed on to the regulator.
operators.sharingCaption: A bank granting consent, and what the association sees under Shared with me. Illustrative data.

terms.title: You set the terms
terms.body: Choose the recipient, which datasets, the purpose, the period, and whether they may view only or also download.

onward.title: Onward sharing only as you allow
onward.body: An association can pass data to a regulator only if you named that regulator, only what you shared, and never further.

revoke.title: Revoke at any time
revoke.body: Change or revoke in a click. Every request is checked against your consent at that moment, so access stops at once.

history.title: A history that can't be rewritten
history.body: Every grant, change, revocation, pass-on and download is recorded in a chained audit history that shows any tampering.

operators.sharingSmall: Recipients register their own organisation account at no cost. Receiving data doesn't give them your plan's features. Exporting your own data and your regulator reports stay on every plan.
operators.plansLead: Per ATM per month, in US dollars, billed by invoice. Two months free on annual terms.

trust.title: Verified institutions, checked claims
trust.body: Before a bank can publish, it proves control of its email domain and someone at the bank, found independently of the applicant, confirms them. Every ATM it adds is checked against the public map and other institutions' listings; a disputed ATM stays off the map until it is resolved. Each decision is recorded in , the GEO network's verification service. It is not a banking licence. Verified once, an institution is recognised across GEO products.
trust.dataBody: Status reports, uploads and findings are seen only by your organisation and the GeoATM team. Other institutions see your ATMs only as locations on the public map, unless you choose to share more on Enterprise, with your consent. Your own uptime, history and regulator reports are on every plan.

faq.q1: Do we need to connect GeoATM to our ATMs?
faq.a1: No. Monitor works from your ATM inventory and the daily status report you already produce, set against the public record of ATMs. Connecting your own monitoring system directly is something we scope with you on Enterprise.
faq.a2: That your organisation controls its email domain, and that someone there, whom we found independently, confirmed you may act for it. It is not a banking licence; where a regulator publishes a list, the register shows that separately.
faq.q3: Can other banks see our data?
faq.a3: Not unless you share it. Your status reports, uploads and findings are yours. Other institutions see your ATMs only as locations on the public map, as you see theirs, and that is all a network comparison uses. On Enterprise you can choose to share chosen datasets with a named organisation, on terms you set and can revoke.
faq.q4: Does an association or regulator pay to receive data we share?
faq.a4: No. Receiving shared data is free; the recipient registers its own organisation account. Analysing it (comparisons, benchmarking, dashboards) needs the recipient's own plan: your Enterprise features are not passed on with the data.
faq.q5: Does sharing replace our regulatory reporting?
faq.a5: No. Your own regulator reports and exports are on every plan, Free included, and disclosures the law requires don't depend on a subscription. Consent-based sharing is for anything you choose to share beyond them.
faq.q6: Does GeoATM alert us when an ATM goes down?
faq.a6: Not by itself: GeoATM isn't connected to your machines. It works from the status reports you upload, flags exceptions in them, and emails your administrators about new findings. Connecting your own monitoring system is something we scope with you on Enterprise.
faq.q7: How is the bill worked out?
faq.a7: Per ATM listed on the 1st of the month, with a monthly minimum, billed by invoice. Annual terms get two months free. Upgrades start straight away; downgrades from the next period; nothing is prorated.
